newsitem.title: PERU: Camet sees investment in Peru up 24 pct '96 vs '95.
newsitem.headline: Camet sees investment in Peru up 24 pct '96 vs '95.

text.p: Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Congress late Wednesday investment spending in Peru this year has increased 24 percent compared to last year.
"In the last three years, investment has grown in real terms at a rate above 20 percent each year and has reached a level of 24 percent in 1996," Camet said.
It was not clear if Camet was giving an estimate for the whole of 1996 or for the year to date.

Since 1988, when the government started tracking foreign investment in Peru, direct foreign investment had risen to $5.722 billion by the end of August, according to the National Commission of Foreign Investment and Technology (CONITE).
Figures for total investment were not available.
Camet added he expected investment in the country to continue increasing at a rate above the government's projected gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate.
The government estimates annual economic growth of between three percent and four percent this year, of five percent next year, and of six percent in the following two years.
In the areas of mining and hydrocarbons alone, the government expects over $10 billion in investment during the next five years, Camet added.
